# Power monitor / distribution - BOM (rev 0, draft)

Written 2026-11-14. Status: DRAFT, not ordered.

**Schematics + authoritative BOM are now in `kicad/`** (generated by
`kicad/gen_schematic.py`, KiCad 8 format):
- `main_board.kicad_sch`, `ct_board.kicad_sch` - open in KiCad 8 or 9
- `main_board_bom_jlcpcb.csv`, `ct_board_bom_jlcpcb.csv` - JLCPCB BOM with
  verified LCSC numbers (`kicad/export_bom.py` regenerates them)
The tables below are the design notes; where they differ, the schematic wins.

Changes made while drawing the schematic (2026-11-14):
- MCU: **STM32G071KBT6N** (LQFP-32, LCSC C529349) instead of CBT6 (LQFP-48):
  the only G071 LQFP symbol in the KiCad library, and 32 pins are enough.
  VDD = VDDA on this package -> one ferrite (FB1) feeds the whole MCU.
  Pin map: PA0 = V, PA1 / PB0 / PB1 / PA5 = CT1-CT4, PB6/PB7 = I2C1
  SCL/SDA, PA8 = CRITICAL (open-drain), PB15 = status LED, PA13/PA14 = SWD,
  PF2 = NRST. Pull-ups on PA3, PA10, PB9 (bootloader USART RX) and PA4
  (SPI1 NSS). **Verify these against AN2606 and the datasheet before layout.**
- Fuse holders: Keystone **3568** (mini blade only, LCSC C5249699) - has a
  KiCad footprint.
- 24 V input terminal: same 5.08 mm 18 A terminal as the outputs (no 7.62 mm
  2-pin footprint in the KiCad library; max input current ~8.5 A).
- Bias 1.65 V: one shared divider (R70/R71 + C30/C31) for all 5 channels.
- Footprints to check against the chosen parts: RJ45 (J20 / CT board J1),
  barrel jack (J21). ZMCT103C needs a custom footprint from its drawing.

## Concept - two boards
| | **CT board** (in the mains area) | **Main board** (next to the Pi) |
|---|---|---|
| Where | Electronics bay, next to the AC inlet / SSRs / PSU | Electronics bay, next to the Pi |
| What | 4 wire-through current transformers + burden resistors + clamps | STM32G071 (mains V/I/W), 3 x INA3221 (24 V / 5 V), fused 24 V / 5 V distribution |
| Mains copper | **None** - mains wires only pass through the CT holes | None - mains voltage via an external AC-AC adapter |
| Link | RJ45 <- shielded Cat6 STP (4 twisted pairs = 4 CTs), <= 1 m -> RJ45 | |

- The Pi reads everything over one I2C bus (`dtparam=i2c_arm=on` is
  already set): INA3221 at 0x40-0x42, STM32G071 as I2C target at 0x50.
- Board 3.3 V from its own LDO (fed from the 5 V input).

### CT board layout and safety rules
- **No copper except the CT secondaries, burdens, TVS and RJ45.** A routed
  slot / keep-out around each CT hole.
- Mains wires pass through from outside, **double-insulated**, strain-relieved
  with cable ties so they cannot slide or touch anything else.
- CT isolation rating assumes intact wire insulation - do not thread bare or
  damaged wire.
- RJ45 shield connected to GND on the main board only (one end).
- 230 V wiring done by someone used to mains wiring.

## Board 2: Main board

### Channel map, DC side (proposal - adjust before layout)
INA3221 shunt full scale 163.84 mV, LSB 40 uV.

| Chip / addr | Ch | Rail / load | Expected max | Fuse | Shunt | Full scale | LSB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| U1 / 0x40 (A0=GND) | 1 | **24 V input** from LRS-200-24 | 8.5 A | - (PSU side) | 10 mOhm | 16.4 A | 4 mA |
| U1 | 2 | 24 V -> Spider (motors + logic + its fans) | 7 A | 10 A | 10 mOhm | 16.4 A | 4 mA |
| U1 | 3 | 24 V -> SB2040 (hotend + toolhead fans) | 3.5 A | 5 A | 20 mOhm | 8.2 A | 2 mA |
| U2 / 0x41 (A0=VS) | 1 | 24 V -> chamber heater fan(s) / bed fans | 1.5 A | 3 A | 50 mOhm | 3.3 A | 0.8 mA |
| U2 | 2 | 24 V -> Nevermore / exhaust | 1.5 A | 3 A | 50 mOhm | 3.3 A | 0.8 mA |
| U2 | 3 | 24 V -> lights (Daylight XXL) | 2 A | 3 A | 20 mOhm | 8.2 A | 2 mA |
| U3 / 0x42 (A0=SDA) | 1 | 24 V -> spare (12 V buck for the PTC fan, ...) | 2 A | 3 A | 20 mOhm | 8.2 A | 2 mA |
| U3 | 2 | **5 V input** (today: Spider 5 V pin; later a dedicated 5 V supply) | 4 A | - | 10 mOhm | 16.4 A | 4 mA |
| U3 | 3 | 5 V -> Pi (+ screen, USB cam via Pi) | 3.5 A | 5 A | 20 mOhm | 8.2 A | 2 mA |

Fan channels use 50 mOhm so a stalled or dead fan (~0.1 A drop) is clearly
visible. Sum check: 24 V input vs. sum of the 24 V outputs.

#### INA3221 26 V limit - mitigation
The INA3221 input common-mode range (and abs max) is 26 V, only ~2 V above
the 24 V rail:
- Set the LRS-200-24 output to 24.0 V (adjustable 21.6-28.8 V), check with
  a multimeter.
- The board sits on the PSU side; motor braking spikes are mostly absorbed
  by the Spider's own bulk capacitors.
- Input RC filter on every channel, bulk capacitance and TVS on the 24 V
  bus (the TVS only catches large spikes - it clamps above 26 V).
- If the rail ever needs to go above 24 V: INA238/INA228 (85 V), rev 1.

### Mains side (signals from the CT board + AC adapter)
**MCU: STM32G071KBT6N** (LQFP-32, 128 KB flash, 12-bit ADC up to 2.5 Msps,
hardware oversampling, internal oscillator - no crystal or external flash).
Samples 4 CT channels + mains voltage at ~4 kHz each; over 10 cycles
(200 ms) computes Vrms, Irms, real power (W), VA, power factor, Hz and
accumulates Wh per channel. Multiplexed sampling (~1 us apart) gives
< 0.1 degree phase error at 50 Hz - negligible.

**Mains voltage (230 V / 50 Hz) without mains on the PCB:** an external
AC-AC wall adapter (transformer type, 9-12 V **AC** output - not a DC
adapter). Its output is divided down and biased to 1.65 V (OpenEnergyMonitor
emonTx method). Calibrate once against a multimeter.

**Firmware updates from the Pi, no extra wires:** the STM32G0 ROM bootloader
supports I2C1 (AN2606). The application implements a "jump to bootloader"
I2C command; the Pi then flashes over the same bus (`stm32flash` supports
I2C). Recovery: SWD header (ST-Link, or OpenOCD on Pi GPIOs) and a BOOT0
solder pad. Notes:
- Use **I2C1 on the pins AN2606 lists for the G07x bootloader** for the
  target interface, so app and bootloader share the bus pins (verify in
  AN2606 before layout).
- Check that the bootloader's fixed I2C address does not collide with
  0x40-0x42 / 0x50 (AN2606).
- Known issue (ST community): G07x/G08x bootloader **V11.3** can get stuck
  polling USART3 while the host uses I2C, stretching SCL. Mitigation: pull-ups
  on all bootloader USART RX pins so they idle high, and keep SWD as fallback.
- BOOT0 is PA14 = SWCLK on the G0 (shared pin); boot selection via option
  bytes (nBOOT_SEL / nBOOT0). Do not hard-wire PA14.

### Main board PCB
- 2 layers, **2 oz copper**, approx. 110 x 90 mm.
- 24 V bus and the input/Spider paths: wide pours on both layers, stitching
  vias (>= 10 A).
- **Kelvin connections** from the inner ends of each shunt pad, routed as a
  pair to the RC filter and the INA.
- Analog section (RJ45, bias, anti-alias, MCU ADC pins) in a separate corner
  away from the high-current pours and fuses; solid GND plane underneath.
- Silkscreen: channel names, fuse ratings, polarity, "24.0 V MAX".

## Software (to do)
- STM32G071 firmware: ADC + DMA at ~4 kHz per channel, RMS/power math over
  10 cycles, I2C target 0x50 with a register map (V, I, W, VA, PF, Hz, Wh
  per channel) and a "jump to bootloader" command.
- Python service on the Pi: reads the 3 INA3221 (0x40-0x42) and the
  STM32 (0x50), publishes to Moonraker (MQTT sensor component) for history
  and Mainsail.
- Checks: 24 V input vs. sum of outputs; fan channel current too low ->
  warning; bed/chamber current while Klipper reports the heater off -> stuck
  SSR -> cut power via the Shelly relay.

## Alert handling - all options available
CRITICAL and WARNING are open-drain, wired-OR lines, so they can go to
several inputs at once. The board supports every reaction; which one is
used is chosen in software/config, not by rewiring:

| Source | Line | Goes to | Possible reaction (configurable) |
|---|---|---|---|
| INA3221 critical limit (per channel, hardware comparator, ~1 ms) | CRITICAL | Spider input (J11) **and** Pi GPIO (J10) | Klipper `[gcode_button]` on the Spider pin: `PAUSE`, `M112` (emergency stop) or log only |
| INA3221 warning limit (averaged) | WARNING | Pi GPIO (J10) | Pi service: log / Mainsail notification / Mobileraker push |
| STM32 mains checks (overcurrent, bed/chamber current outside expected range) | CRITICAL (open-drain GPIO) | same as above | same as above - works even if the Pi service is not running |
| Pi service (stuck SSR: current while Klipper reports heater off) | - (software) | Moonraker + Shelly | cut mains via the Shelly relay, `M112` via Moonraker |

Limits for the INA critical/warning comparators and the STM32 checks are
written over I2C by the Pi service at start-up (stored in a config file),
so they can be changed without reflashing.

## 5 V supply note
Today the Pi is fed from the Spider's 5 V pin. The board measures whatever
feeds the 5 V input, so nothing changes in the design. Recommended later:
a dedicated 5 V supply (e.g. Mean Well LRS-35-5 / LRS-50-5 or a 24 V -> 5 V
5 A DIN buck) into the 5 V input - takes the Pi + screen + USB cam load off
the Spider's regulator and avoids Pi brown-outs.

## Decisions
- 2026-11-14: mains voltage measured via AC-AC adapter (230 V / 50 Hz).
- 2026-11-14: two boards (CT board + main board), STM32G071 instead of RP2350B.
- 2026-11-14: JLCPCB assembly (prefer Basic parts).
- 2026-11-14: all alert reactions supported (log / pause / emergency stop / Shelly cut), chosen in config.
